newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish BDM brokerage underwrites Centrostal IPO.
newsitem.headline: Polish BDM brokerage underwrites Centrostal IPO.

text.p: Polish brokerage Beskidzki Dom Maklerski SA (BDM) has underwritten 40 percent of Polish steel products trader Centrostal SA's one-million-share initial public offering due in December, Centrostal's finance director said.
BDM is underwriting 400,000 shares for a standby fee of two percent in the December 9 to December 20 offering. All of the one million shares must be taken to make the issue valid.
"It would be a shame if for example there was a lack of 20 registerings for shares and the issue failed," Jerzy Ilkiewicz told Reuters on Thursday.
BDM will receive an additional three percent if it needs to take up shares, the minimum price for which is 4.1 zlotys each.
Ilkiewicz said the firm preferred a main-market listing but that it was not yet clear if the shareholder structure would be too concentrated for the main floor.
After Stalexport, BDM has 13.6 percent of Centrostal, with Stalexport in turn holding about 20 percent of BDM.
Last month Centrostal said the firm expected a parallel-market listing but could reach the main market in the second half of 1997.
Centrostal netted 1.5 million zlotys over the first 10 months this year on sales of 85.7 million zlotys.
It expects to net two million zlotys this year and 2.3 million zlotys next year against 1.8 million in 1995.
It sees sales rising to 103.9 million zlotys this year and 112.8 million in 1997 from last year's 78.6 million.
